story:
Nanabozho, a spirit of the Ojibwe people, is one of four sons born to a human mother and a spirit father called E-bangishimog ("In the West"). Nanabozho is a shapeshifter, able to take the form of male or female animals or humans, though he most often appears as a rabbit, called Mishaabooz ("Great rabbit") or Gitchii-waabooz ("Big rabbit"). He was sent to Earth by Gitche Manidoo to teach the Ojibwe people. One of his first tasks upon arriving was to name all the plants and animals. He is credited as the founder of the Midewiwin, and as the inventor of fishing and of hieroglyphs. As a co-creator of the world, he is called Michabo Ovisaketchak, "the Great Hare who created the Earth." As a trickster, Nanabozho often creates chaos, being greedy and manipulative, but through forming deep relationships with others he becomes more balanced.

In a later legend, Nanabozho encounters the lumberjack Paul Bunyan, who has been cutting down forests across the land. Nanabozho confronts Bunyan in Minnesota and asks him to leave without logging any more timber. The two fight for forty days and forty nights. Nanabozho ends the battle by slapping Bunyan across the face with a Red Lake walleye fish. Bunyan stumbles, and Nanabozho pulls at his whiskers, forcing him to promise to leave the area. In another version of the story, Bunyan falls onto his rear end at the fight's end, and the shape of his buttocks creates Lake Bemidji.
